questions.stem: E[X] = 2 and E[X²] = 13. What is Var(X)?
questions.correctFeedback: Right — mean of the square minus square of the mean: 13 − 2² = 9.

questions.stem: What does Chebyshev's inequality need to hold?
options: a normal, bell-shaped distribution of X
a symmetric distribution around its mean
a large sample of observed values
only a finite mean and variance
questions.correctFeedback: Right — it works for every shape, which is exactly why it's loose.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Chebyshev needs only a finite mean and variance. No normality, no symmetry, no sample size.

questions.stem: Mean 20, variance 16, shape unknown. A lower bound for P(12 < X < 28) is…
questions.correctFeedback: Correct — σ = 4, so 8 = 2σ and the bound is 1 − 1/4 = 3/4.

questions.stem: From Lesson 6: for a fair die, how does E[X²] compare with (3.5)²?
questions.correctFeedback: Yes — E[X²] = 91/6 ≈ 15.17 > 12.25. The gap is the die's variance, 35/12.
questions.incorrectFeedback: The average of the squares always beats the square of the average unless X never varies: 91/6 ≈ 15.17 > 12.25.
